newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan's Sharif seeks better ties with India.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan's Sharif seeks better ties with India.

text.p: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif said on Friday he wanted to improve ties with arch-rival India, the official news agency APP reported.

It quoted Sharif as saying that he "shared the commitment of his Indian counterpart Inder Kumar Gujral to improving relations between the two countries" and looked forward to meeting him at a regional summit in the Maldives capital Male next month.
Sharif was speaking at a meeting with Indian High Commissioner (ambassador) Satish Chandra, who handed over a message from Gujral.
"With each of us showing a constructive and forward-looking approach we are confident that our exchanges will be useful and lead to mutually beneficial results," Gujral's message said.
Senior Indian and Pakistani foreign ministry officials held talks in New Delhi in March after a gap of more than three years in formal contacts between the South Asian neighbours.
A second round of talks is expected to take place in Islamabad in early May.

India and Pakistan have fought three wars since independence from Britain in 1947, two of them over the divided Himalayan territory of Kashmir. The Kashmir dispute remains the main obstacle to ending hostility between the two countries.
